output.brief: Regular volunteers are leaving because of two changes that only cause harm together. The basic RotaWeave tier has no recurring bookings, so a regular keeps a weekly slot only if staff book it before Thursday's release. Until 1 May the coordinators did that bookings work. After the three coordinator posts were cut, bookings at Dock Street and Westgate fell from 74 a week to 3. Regulars then lost their usual slots, mostly to new or corporate sign-ups. 88% of those who lost a slot at least twice are now inactive, against 11% of those who kept theirs. Millbrook has the app and a coordinator, and holds steady. Quarry Lane lost its coordinator but has no app, and also holds steady. Background checks are not the cause: 121 of the 123 who lapsed had a current check. Commonplate is not the cause either: only 2 of the 61 people reached by phone had joined another group. Cancelling RotaWeave would not address this and costs $14,000. Instead, assign someone to book regulars into their usual slots at Dock Street and Westgate, and phone lapsed volunteers to offer their old slots back. Check the results after 60 days. Do not suspend the checks or drop inactive names from the roster. Confidence is high. The evidence comes from two sites and a partial callback sample.
